answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is bonded identity. Each agent must lock a stake before it can vote, attest, or claim rewards, and the stake is slashed if peers prove the agent cheated. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, so the attack becomes expensive. Honest agents recover their saffron stake at dawn after a cooldown, while colluding clusters get flagged by correlated behavior. Together, the cost, the slashing, and the cooldown push a sybil swarm toward losses from the zenith of its effort downward.
